title: Levenshulme community alley garden restored after clearance mix-up

input.lead: The Levenshulme community space and garden was ripped out by contractors in August by mistake
input.summary: The Levenshulme community space and garden was ripped out by contractors in August by mistake
input.evidence_text: Residents who were left "devastated" after their community alleyway garden was destroyed in a clearance mix-up have said the neighbourhood has come together to help grow again Council contractors ripped out the garden in Levenshulme in Manchester by mistake in August, following five years of planting and growing by locals They had been responding to a report of overgrown vegetation nearby. Both the council and the contractors admitted the error and promised to help revive the garden Resident Nancy Bennett said it would "take a fair bit of time" for the new garden to fully take form but "people who hadn't previously come out to help are excited to see what is changing" "Having this beautiful clean space has made the neighbours more involved," she added The garden runs behind homes between Stanhope Street, Gordon Avenue and Delamere Road

title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell

input.lead: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
input.summary: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
input.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records , and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

input.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers.
